RECONCILED BY HAND, not reported by tubuild's conflict detector, which compares declaration spellings rather than types. (1) data_0209d45c and data_0209d454 arrived both as `unsigned char x[]` (func_ov003_020b060c) and as `u8 x` (InitResources) -- an array against a scalar, a hard compile error once merged. The scalar won, matching the rest of the tree and include/dScMgBase_c.h's prose; the two `[0]` subscripts became scalar reads. (2) func_ov003_020b060c was defined `void func_ov003_020b060c(char *)` against include/decl_common.h:2301's `extern void func_ov003_020b060c(void*);` -- `illegal function overloading`, reported against the definition line and never naming the header. The header won; the `char *` view is kept as a local alias so the raw-offset accesses keep their legacy spelling. (3) The legacy shadow types `VT`/`Obj` collided with include/decl_common.h:415's real ROM symbol `extern int VT[];`, which a variable-hides-a-tag lookup turns into `undefined identifier 'VT'` on the struct that uses it. Renamed to GameOverGateVt/GameOverGate; they are file-local shadow types with no ROM identity.

The blast radius `create` warns about was measured, not assumed: with it set, all 9 members MATCH, so it costs the other eight nothing.
